question: Which of the following enzymes is found in the saliva of the human body which breaks down starch into simple sugar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amylase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Amylase__

 __
 
• It is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of starch into sugars.
 
• All amylases are glycoside hydrolases.
 
• alpha and beta amylases are important in brewing beer and liquor made from sugars derived from starch.
 
• Amylases are used in breadmaking and to break down complex sugars, such as starch into simple sugars.
 
• Saccharides are a food source rich in energy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Protease

 
 
• A protease is an enzyme that catalyzes proteolysis.
 
• Protease occurs in all organisms from prokaryotes to eukaryotes to viruses.
 
• It is involved in many biological functions, including digestion of ingested proteins, protein catabolism, and cell signaling.
 
• Protease is used to make Paneer.
 
• Proteases are used in industry, medicine, and basic biological research.
 
 
 
• Lipase
 
 
• Lipase is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of fats (lipids)
 
• Lipases perform essential roles in digestion transport and processing of dietary lipids.
 
• The main lipases of the human digestive system are pancreatic lipase and pancreatic lipase-related protein 2.
 
• Lipases are a subclass of the esterases.
 
 
 
• Peptidase
 
 
• It is an enzyme that breaks down peptides into amino acids.
 
• It is produced in the stomach, small intestine, and pancreas.
